indicator_neutral_fallback.name: Indicator Neutral Fallback Scoring
indicator_neutral_fallback.pattern: When indicators return None/NaN, use neutral defaults (50) not zero
indicator_neutral_fallback.problem: Zero-value fallbacks in signal_engine.py caused the weighted average composite score to collapse below MIN_GEM_SCORE, blocking ALL trades even for legitimate micro-cap gems

solution.approach: Replace all 0-value defaults with 50 (neutral midpoint) across RSI, MACD, Bollinger, and custom indicators
solution.key_insight: 50 represents 'no data available, assume average' — it doesn't boost or penalize the score

quality_rules: Never use 0 as a fallback for any indicator that feeds into a weighted average
Always explicitly handle None/NaN returns from indicator functions
Test composite scoring with ALL indicators returning None to verify minimum viable score

manus_import_verification.name: Manus Edit Import Verification
manus_import_verification.pattern: After merging any Manus AI changes, verify all imports are intact and no undefined variables were introduced
manus_import_verification.problem: Manus sometimes introduces variable references without corresponding imports, or removes imports during refactoring. This causes NameError at runtime that only surfaces in Docker on Hetzner.

solution.approach: After every Manus merge: 1) grep for undefined names, 2) run `python -c 'import module'` for each changed file, 3) check top-level imports match all references
solution.key_insight: Manus operates on partial context — it can't see the full import tree

quality_rules: Always `python -c 'import <module>'` after Manus changes before committing
Check for NameError specifically — it's the most common Manus regression
Review the diff carefully for removed imports that are still referenced elsewhere

solana_wallet_routing.name: Solana vs EVM Wallet Routing
solana_wallet_routing.pattern: Solana uses keypair file paths, EVM uses private key hex strings — wallet router must dispatch correctly
solana_wallet_routing.problem: Passing a hex private key to the Solana executor causes a silent failure. Passing a keypair path to an EVM executor causes a ValueError.

solution.approach: wallet_router.py dispatches based on chain type: Solana → keypair JSON path from SOLANA_WALLET_PATH env var; EVM → private key hex from chain-specific env var (BASE_PRIVATE_KEY, BSC_PRIVATE_KEY, etc.)
solution.key_insight: The chain → wallet mapping must be explicit, never inferred

quality_rules: Always check chain type before selecting wallet credentials
Solana keypair paths must point to actual JSON files on disk
EVM private keys must be 64-char hex (with or without 0x prefix)

docker_rebuild_after_python_changes.name: Docker Rebuild Required After Python Changes
docker_rebuild_after_python_changes.pattern: Any Python file change requires `docker compose build --no-cache` before `docker compose up -d` on Hetzner
docker_rebuild_after_python_changes.problem: Docker caches Python layers. A simple `docker compose restart` will run the OLD code. The --no-cache flag ensures the COPY step re-runs.

solution.approach: Always use the full rebuild cycle: `docker compose down && docker compose build --no-cache && docker compose up -d`
solution.key_insight: The Dockerfile COPY . . step is cached — without --no-cache, code changes are invisible

quality_rules: Never use `docker compose restart` for code changes — only for config/env changes
Always verify with `docker compose logs -f --tail=20 bot` after rebuild
Check the build output to confirm the COPY step ran (not cached)

env_provisioning_backup.name: Always Backup .env Before Git Pull
env_provisioning_backup.pattern: Always backup the Hetzner .env file before `git pull` — deployment regressions can wipe it
env_provisioning_backup.problem: A `git pull` or `git checkout` can overwrite or delete the .env file on the server, wiping all API keys, wallet keys, and RPCs. This bricked the entire multi-chain trading setup.

solution.approach: Before any git operation on Hetzner: `cp .env .env.backup.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)`
solution.key_insight: .env is in .gitignore but git operations can still affect it during merges or resets

quality_rules: ALWAYS `cp .env .env.backup` before git pull on production servers
Keep a master copy of all env vars in a secure location (not git)
Verify .env exists and has correct line count after any git operation

min_gem_score_threshold_tuning.name: MIN_GEM_SCORE Must Account for Data Scarcity
min_gem_score_threshold_tuning.pattern: MIN_GEM_SCORE of 50 requires that micro-cap tokens with limited data can still reach 50 through fallback scoring alone
min_gem_score_threshold_tuning.problem: New micro-cap tokens have no price history, no social signals, and limited Moralis data. If the scoring formula defaults missing data to 0, even the best gems score 20-30 and never trade.

solution.approach: Ensure each scoring component has a fallback that produces a 'pass the bar' score when data is unavailable. The composite of all neutrals (50) should equal exactly MIN_GEM_SCORE.
solution.key_insight: The threshold and the fallback defaults are a coupled system — change one, check the other

quality_rules: After changing MIN_GEM_SCORE, simulate scoring with all-None indicators
After changing any indicator weight, verify the all-neutral composite still passes
Log the component breakdown when a token is rejected for score

evm_chain_poa_middleware.name: BSC and Non-Mainnet EVM Chains Need PoA Middleware
evm_chain_poa_middleware.pattern: BSC, Avalanche, and other non-Ethereum-mainnet EVM chains require geth_poa_middleware injected into the Web3 instance
evm_chain_poa_middleware.problem: Without PoA middleware, Web3.py raises ExtraDataLengthError on BSC/AVAX blocks because the extraData field exceeds the mainnet spec.

solution.approach: Inject `geth_poa_middleware` at layer 0 for any non-Ethereum-mainnet chain in executor.py
solution.key_insight: This is a Web3.py-specific issue — ethers.js handles it automatically

quality_rules: Always inject PoA middleware for BSC, AVAX, and any PoA-consensus chain
Test with a simple `w3.eth.get_block('latest')` call after provider setup

position_monitor_function_signatures.name: Position Monitor Function Call Signatures
position_monitor_function_signatures.pattern: When calling functions from offensive_guardrails.py in position_monitor.py, always match the exact parameter signature — especially `get_dynamic_trailing_stop_pct(pos, base_pct, state)`
position_monitor_function_signatures.problem: Calling `get_dynamic_trailing_stop_pct(pos, base_pct)` without the `state` parameter caused incorrect trailing stop calculations, leading to premature exits.

solution.approach: Pass the offensive state object to all offensive guardrail functions that need it
solution.key_insight: The offensive state carries God Mode status which can tighten stops further

quality_rules: Always check function signatures when calling across modules
Use IDE hints or grep for the function definition before calling
Test trailing stop values in paper mode before deploying

dedup_guard_trade_spam.name: Deduplication Guard for Repeated Trade Attempts
dedup_guard_trade_spam.pattern: Without a dedup guard, the bot will attempt to buy the same token on every scan cycle, wasting gas and hitting rate limits
dedup_guard_trade_spam.problem: Failed trades (slippage, insufficient liquidity) were retried every 60 seconds indefinitely, burning gas fees and flooding API endpoints.

solution.approach: Maintain a cooldown dict of recently attempted tokens with a configurable TTL (default 30 minutes). Skip any token in cooldown.
solution.key_insight: The cooldown should apply to both successful and failed attempts

quality_rules: Cooldown must persist across scan cycles but NOT across bot restarts
Log when a token is skipped due to cooldown (for debugging)
Different cooldown durations for success (longer) vs failure (shorter)

moralis_timeframe_parameter.name: Moralis API Timeframe Parameter Validation
moralis_timeframe_parameter.pattern: Moralis getFilteredTokens timeframe parameter must be a valid enum value — invalid values return 200 OK with wrong data, not an error
moralis_timeframe_parameter.problem: Passing incorrect timeframe values (e.g., '24h' instead of '1d') silently returns data from an unexpected timeframe, producing misleading metrics.

solution.approach: Validate timeframe against the documented enum before making API calls. Valid values: '5m', '15m', '30m', '1h', '4h', '12h', '1d', '1w', '1M'
solution.key_insight: Moralis does not return errors for invalid enum values — it silently defaults

quality_rules: Always validate enum parameters against documented values before API calls
Log the actual timeframe used in each request for auditability
Test with known data to verify the response matches the expected timeframe

float_boundary_tolerance.name: Float Comparison Boundary Tolerance
float_boundary_tolerance.pattern: Never compare float percentages with exact equality or boundary checks — always add epsilon tolerance
float_boundary_tolerance.problem: Python float arithmetic: (0.90 - 1.0) / 1.0 * 100 = -9.9999999999998, which is NOT <= -10.0. Hard stop at exactly -10% never fired.

solution.approach: Add +0.001% tolerance on all percentage boundary comparisons: `if pnl_pct <= -(hard_stop_pct - 0.001)`
solution.key_insight: This is a classic IEEE 754 trap — unit tests caught it before production lost money

quality_rules: Never use `<=` or `>=` on computed floats without epsilon tolerance
Always unit test boundary conditions with exact threshold values
For percentage comparisons, 0.001% tolerance is sufficient

strategy_profile_pipeline_wiring.name: Strategy Profile Must Flow Through Entire Pipeline
strategy_profile_pipeline_wiring.pattern: Per-wallet strategy profiles must be stored at registration and resolved at every evaluation point — or they silently fall back to global defaults
strategy_profile_pipeline_wiring.problem: StrategyProfile was defined in wallets.py but never passed through register_position() or consumed by evaluate_position(). Nuclear Wallet B's 5x/12x/30x TP ladder was completely ignored.

solution.approach: Store strategy_profile.name in position data at registration, use _PROFILE_MAP in monitor to resolve the full object, pass to evaluate_position()
solution.key_insight: Infrastructure code built in isolation can sit unconnected for weeks without anyone noticing — always trace the data flow end-to-end

quality_rules: When adding new per-position metadata, verify it flows: creation → storage → monitoring → exit
Use substring matching for dynamic reason strings (e.g., 'tp1_' not 'tp1_2x')
Always test with at least 2 profile variants to catch hardcoded assumptions

hyperliquid_symbol_normalization.name: Hyperliquid Symbol Normalization
hyperliquid_symbol_normalization.pattern: Hyperliquid uses unwrapped symbols (ETH not WETH, BTC not WBTC). Must strip 'W' prefix before placing orders.
hyperliquid_symbol_normalization.problem: Submitting an order for 'WETH' or 'WBTC' on Hyperliquid fails silently — no matching perp market. The SDK returns an error but no assets are lost.

solution.approach: Build a normalization map: WETH→ETH, WBTC→BTC, WMATIC→MATIC, WAVAX→AVAX, etc. Apply before any order placement.
solution.key_insight: CEX/DEX perp venues use different symbol conventions than on-chain DEXes

quality_rules: Always normalize token symbols before sending to any perp venue
Maintain a lookup table of wrapped→unwrapped mappings
Log the normalized symbol so debugging is clear

perp_capital_protection_layers.name: Multi-Layer Capital Protection for Leveraged Perps
perp_capital_protection_layers.pattern: Leveraged perps require at least 6 independent protection layers to prevent capital loss
perp_capital_protection_layers.problem: A single stop-loss is insufficient for leveraged trading. Adverse funding rates, daily drawdown spirals, and correlation risk all bypass simple TP/SL.

solution.approach: Implement: (1) per-trade % SL/TP, (2) per-trade account risk cap (10%), (3) daily loss circuit breaker, (4) funding rate safety check, (5) min gem score gate, (6) max concurrent positions + total exposure cap
solution.key_insight: Each layer catches a different failure mode. Combined, they make capital loss require 6 simultaneous failures.

quality_rules: New execution venues MUST have at least: SL, TP, daily loss limit, per-trade risk cap
Always start with lowest reasonable leverage (2x) and scale up only with proven track record
Circuit breaker should halt ALL trading for the day, not just the venue

erc8021_builder_code_attribution.name: Base ERC-8021 Builder Code Attribution
erc8021_builder_code_attribution.pattern: Register wallets with Base builder code API and append ERC-8021 data suffix to every Base chain transaction
erc8021_builder_code_attribution.problem: Without builder code attribution, on-chain activity is invisible to Base's tracking system. No errors — just silent, permanent invisibility.

solution.approach: One-time registration via POST to api.base.dev. Encode builder code as UTF-8 hex + magic bytes + length. Append to tx data field only for chain=='base'.
solution.key_insight: Zero gas overhead — the suffix is just extra calldata. Free to add, potentially valuable for builder incentive programs.

quality_rules: NEVER re-register a wallet — it generates a new code and breaks the old one
Builder codes are per-wallet, not per-chain or per-app
Attribution must be wired into ALL Base transaction paths (1inch, Flashbots, direct)

parallel_execution_venue_isolation.name: Execution Venue Isolation Principle
parallel_execution_venue_isolation.pattern: New execution venues must run as isolated parallel systems with their own wallets, risk limits, and circuit breakers
parallel_execution_venue_isolation.problem: Sharing state (e.g. daily PnL, position counts) between on-chain and perp venues creates correlation risk and makes circuit breakers unreliable.

solution.approach: Each venue gets: its own wallet, its own daily PnL tracker, its own position counter, its own circuit breaker. Only share the signal pipeline.
solution.key_insight: Isolation means a bad day on-chain doesn't cascade to perps and vice versa

quality_rules: New execution venues should be self-contained modules with no shared mutable state
Daily loss limits are per-venue, not global
Log venue name in all trade-related log messages for clear attribution

todo_comments_are_blockers.name: TODO Comments Are Silent Blockers
todo_comments_are_blockers.pattern: TODO/FIXME comments in production code represent untracked work items — they must be surfaced as blockers or tracked in task.md
todo_comments_are_blockers.problem: reconciliation.py had a docstring saying 'EVM reconciliation can follow the same pattern' but it was never implemented. The gap went unnoticed for weeks.

solution.approach: Grep for TODO/FIXME/HACK in the codebase periodically. Convert any critical ones into tracked tasks. Implement or delete — never leave in limbo.
solution.key_insight: Docstring promises are technical debt that compounds silently

quality_rules: After major feature work, grep `TODO|FIXME|HACK` and resolve or track each one
Never commit a TODO for production-critical functionality — implement it or create an issue
During wiring audits, check that every module's docstring promises match reality
